## Access — behind the gateway door

Who may enter: signed-in members of 👑 Jarl’s Court (`owner`), 🌿 Vale Circle (`vale`). Sign-in is Firebase Authentication in `researcher-455022`; a person's groups are the
custom claim `groups`, granted only with the monorepo's `node scripts/grant-groups.mjs` (docs/runbooks/platform-auth.md).
Access note: Vale reaches Jordan’s grocery account and card: only the listed groups pass, enforced by the gateway door.

- Hosting rewrites `/vale{,/**}` to Cloud Run `gateway` (the gateway door), not to `vale`. The door opens the
  browser's sealed `__session`, re-checks its groups against the current registry, then forwards the full path to https://vale-382031913173.us-central1.run.app.
- Entering: `POST /vale/__door/session` with `Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>` → 200 and a sealed `__session`
  cookie (`Path=/vale`, HttpOnly, at most 12 h) · 401 `sign_in_required` · 403 `group_required`.
  `DELETE /vale/__door/session` leaves. The portal does this for you when you walk through the gate.
- Refusals: a page load (GET with `Accept: text/html`) is redirected 303 to
  `/?gate=vale&reason=<sign_in_required|group_required|session_expired|door_unconfigured>`; any other request gets JSON 401/403/503.
- Gateway API: `https://eisensoftware.com/api/vale/…` needs `Authorization: Bearer <ID token>` that passes the same policy; only
  `https://eisensoftware.com/api/vale/health` stays public.
- The app still sets its own `__session` (contract rule 3): the door keeps it inside the sealed envelope and hands it back
  on every request, so keep its value under about 2 KB.

## Smoke tests

```bash
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://vale-382031913173.us-central1.run.app/vale/   # direct host → 200 while it allows allUsers, 403 after step h
curl -sS https://vale-382031913173.us-central1.run.app/vale/api/health   # health → 200 {"status":"ok","app":"vale",…} while it allows allUsers, 403 after step h
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' -H 'accept: text/html' https://eisensoftware.com/vale/   # no door session → 303 …/?gate=vale&reason=sign_in_required
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://eisensoftware.com/vale/   # the same without accept: text/html → 401 JSON
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://eisensoftware.com/api/vale/health   # the guarded app's one public API route → 200
```

## How to interact

- Browser-session auth: sign in through the browser first; with curl, reuse a saved cookie jar (`-b cookies.txt`). An unauthenticated call is redirected to sign-in or answered 401.
- Through the platform, sign in to eisensoftware.com first and walk through the Vale gate; the portal opens the door for the browser. Without a
  platform session, use the direct host (with `Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-identity-token)` once `allUsers` is gone).
- Every path the app serves lives under `/vale` on both hosts (Hosting passes the full path through). Locally, run with the base path set and open `http://localhost:<port>/vale/`.
- Platform contract v1 (site-plugin skill) applies: relative redirects, all browser state in one `__session` cookie with `Path=/vale`, a health route answering `{"status","app","version","commit","deployedAt"}`, and deploys that set `APP_VERSION`, `APP_COMMIT` and `APP_DEPLOYED_AT` with `--update-env-vars`.
- Source of truth: the `vale` entry in `registry/registry.json` (URLs, status, api, access, repo); CI patches its `deployment` block from the version and commit the health route reports (every 30 minutes) or from a `register-app` call. Edit the registry, then rerun `node plugins/eisen-platform/skills/site-plugin/scripts/generate-site-skills.mjs`.
